identity.title: Foreign Material Exclusion Device Found in Containment Spray System

cause.proximate_text: inadequate instructions for the control of internal foreign material exclusion devices within the valve maintenance procedure; the valve repair team failed to use the internal closure device log during V07162 valve repairs, and a subsequent scope change to perform valve lapping did not prompt review of the FME risk determination and checklist
cause.theme: inadequate FME procedure guidance / missed scope-change review

nodes.display_name: Isolation Valve V07162 (Penetration P-35B, Outside Containment Feed from Shutdown Cooling HX 2A)

properties.description: 12-in manually operated Pacific Gate Valve, horizontal stem, stainless steel body, ANSI class 300, normally locked open during power operations

nodes.display_name: Internal closure device log not used during valve repairs
nodes.description: Valve repair team concluded the internal closure device log was not required based on the original inspection scope, which did not require FME devices.

nodes.display_name: Scope change to valve lapping not reviewed against FME risk determination
nodes.description: A subsequent scope change to perform valve lapping did not prompt the valve repair team to review the FME risk determination and checklist; the crew failed to recognize the need for the internal closure device log.

nodes.display_name: FME device left inside valve body
nodes.description: A 12-inch diameter foam circle with a 6-ft rope lanyard was left inside the valve body of V07162 following maintenance in the previous refueling outage.

nodes.display_name: 2A containment spray train inoperable / flow blockage
Revise valve lapping procedure to have separate sign-off steps for each FME device installation and removal

chain: inadequate FME procedure guidance [cause A] -> internal closure device log not used during valve repairs -> scope change to lapping not reviewed -> FME device (foam circle w/ lanyard) left inside valve body -> 2A containment spray train flow blockage / inoperable (~17.5 months) [no impact on health/safety per UFSAR analysis; fan coolers provide diverse depressurization]
notes: No 'Similar Events' referenced (narrative states 'None'), so no stub LER/SIMILAR_TO edge emitted. UFSAR Table 6.2-41 and fan cooler discussion is design/safety-analysis context supporting the no-impact conclusion; fan coolers are not modeled as an operable backup system per rule 6 since they are cited in a Safety Significance/UFSAR passage, not as a stated-operable backup during the inoperability window. The 2B train surveillance-induced brief inoperabilities are noted in the narrative but the system remained available and promptly returnable to service, so no separate FailureMode/Consequence was created for 2B; only the 2A blockage-driven inoperability period is modeled per the reported condition prohibited by Tech Specs.
